name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male Levite known specifically as the son of Zadok, situating him within the priestly tribe of Levi. His identity is primarily established through this familial connection, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:11. There are no additional notes or distinguishing attributes provided beyond this lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam is a proper name meaning 'restitution.' This meaning, while not explicitly tied to divine naming, reflects a concept of restoration or compensation. The biblical record does not provide additional titles or names for Meshullam beyond this.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Meshullam as the son of Zadok and infers Hilkiah as his father, both noted in Nehemiah 11:11. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are recorded, limiting our understanding of his broader lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance in the biblical narrative is anchored in his role as a descendant of Zadok within the Levitical priesthood, a lineage associated with faithful service to God. This connection places him within the restored community of Israel during the post-exilic period, emphasizing continuity in priestly heritage. Although details about his personal deeds are not provided, his mention affirms the ongoing importance of the Zadokite line in maintaining covenantal worship.
